| Issue (most important) | State‑wide all adults (%) | Los Angeles (%) | Central Valley (%) |
|-------------------------|--------------------------|-----------------|-------------------|
| Jobs, economy | 18 % | 20 % | 18 % |
| Immigration, illegal immigration | 15 % | 11 % | 15 % |
| Housing costs & availability | 9 % | 21 % | 7 % |

*Source: PPIC “Statewide Survey – Most Important Issues” (PDF, page 14, 2018)*【4†L1-L7】.

---

### Step 1 – Issues >9 % statewide

Only **Jobs & the economy** (18 %) and **Immigration** (15 %) exceed 9 % at the state level.  
*Housing* is exactly 9 % (not “over” 9 %) and thus excluded.

---

### Step 2 – Identify an issue that is

* >12 % of Los Angeles respondents named it as the top issue  
* 10–14 % of Central Valley respondents named it as the top issue  

Checking the percentages:

| Issue | Los Angeles | Central Valley |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| Jobs, economy | **20 %** (✓ >12 %) | **18 %** (✗ >14 %) |
| Immigration | **11 %** (✗ >12 %) | **15 %** (✗ 10‑14 %) |
| Housing | **21 %** (✓ >12 %) | **7 %** (✗ 10‑14 %) |

No issue meets both conditions simultaneously. The only overlap is **Jobs & the economy**, which is >12 % in Los Angeles but >14 % in the Central Valley (not within the 10‑14 % window).

---

## Answer

There is **no issue** that satisfies the stated criteria from the PPIC 2018 statewide survey. Only “Jobs & the economy” exceeds 12 % in Los Angeles, but its Central Valley share is 18 % (above 14 %). No issue is between 10 % and 14 % in the Central Valley while also surpassing 12 % in Los Angeles.
